name: Vail Orsmere
aliases: the line that does not balance

identity.realm: Ordinal one, the floor, and there is no gate involved in it at all. A vitrified body has no meridian, no circulation and no dantian, because glass is not a conduit, so qi is shut because glass does not conduct, body is shut because there is nothing left in the body to temper, and mind is shut because the tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue that is being replaced. None of the three was closed by anything she did. Unaffiliated is not the least share of a casting here; it is the only sentence available about her species, and she is inside the last cohort on the one cold dry mineral-rich mountain where the silicate replacement could still proceed.

appearance.presentation: A woman in human proportions, standing outside a public forge in a valley that owns no mountain, which is the first thing about the picture that is wrong and the last thing anybody there can explain. To the temple she is a person; to the temple's own doctrine she is the doctrine's conclusion reached chemically; to the guild that sells the tier's only dense material she is a quantity of it. She is not presenting any of these and is not aware of being the difference between them. Up close the replacement does not stop at the silhouette, because it has taken the fingers, the hairline and both ears, and it is going to take the rest on a date that a different household on a different mountain keeps in a clerk's hand.
appearance.age: The last viable cohort. She is old enough to remember the temple's book being kept in one hand and copied by three boys, and young enough that the copyists are dead, which is the only claim to age her species allows anybody. A vitrified body does not age and there is nothing in her that would show it if it did. Her cohort vitrified before it could breed, so she is the reason there is nobody after her, and nobody has been born since the night the law moved.
appearance.build: Unchanged since the casting that made her, which is not the same as unchanged. Human in proportion and rigid where the replacement has run: the shoulders no longer articulate and she turns the whole frame rather than the head. The same height, the same width and the same weight she has always had, and every gram of it is a substance the temple sells by weight, which is the single fact that makes her impossible to appraise and impossible to price.
appearance.complexion: Clear to the point of being a depth rather than a colour, with a green cast in the thicker sections and a warm internal reflection at the throat that no skin behind it explains. Where the replacement has not yet reached she is entirely ordinary: mid tone, fine, freckled at the shoulder, alive. The line between the two is not a wound and not a scar. It is the boundary between a person and the material that has replaced her, and it is the same boundary the doctrine in this valley draws around every socket it opens.
appearance.hair: Black going silver from the ends inward, and the silver part is glass now, so it holds its shape, takes the light in a hard line, and does not move when she moves her head. It has been cut three times and each time the reason given was that a length had begun to catch on a door frame, which on a body that cannot be moved by two people is not a small fault.
appearance.eyes: The only part of her nobody has ever reported a problem with and the only part with nobody behind it. A vitrified body scans as present and inert: the soul is there, it reads as sitting in a body, and it does not answer. Her eyes have followed a person across a room correctly for as long as anyone has watched, and she has never once been able to report whether she followed anything, which in a valley whose entire practice is the public performance of a rite is the one fact nobody can use.
appearance.palette: Cold clear glass against forge-light, and the whole picture is the argument between the two temperatures. Above the line: no colour at all, hard specular highlights, green in the thick sections, the flame refracted rather than reflected. Below it: ordinary flesh, ordinary warmth, a freckled shoulder. The temple's cloth is undyed because dye has to be accounted for and there is no column for it, so she wears the same grey as the household that has never once had to decide whether she is a person in it.
appearance.attire: A single undyed grey wool over-layer, high-collared, long-sleeved, fastened to the throat and closed at the wrist, because the valley is cold and because the temple's rule is that nothing is left loose that could be pulled. It is fastened with two bone toggles rather than thread, because thread is a consumable and the temple counts consumables. It is the garment she was vitrified in and the only garment anybody here has told her she may wear.
appearance.marks: The replacement itself is the mark: vitreous, running from the extremities inward, past the fingertips, the hairline and both ears, standing as a line across the upper chest with the rest of her untouched beneath it. Nothing has been added. No household mark, no burial mark, no name on any stone, because the temple's register is a book and a book is the one thing in this valley that is corrected in public.
appearance.bearing: Careful, in a way that reads as frailty and is not: a body that has stopped articulating at the shoulders learns to move the whole frame instead of a part of it, so she turns by the hip and pauses between movements rather than at them. She stands where she can see the forge mouth and be seen by anyone coming out of it, which is the posture of somebody who has been told to wait and intends to be findable while waiting.

canon.role_in_story: A plains faith holds that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, and it enacts that once, publicly, for a fee: worked ore from the temple's own face, a socket cemented in the public forge with no hood over the furnace, and a line in a book that is read aloud. Everything else in the doctrine is prohibition. No socket may be opened once sealed and reforging one is the single act the temple's own forge is not permitted to perform, because a second seal is how the Iron Grief happened, and opening a living body is forbidden absolutely. Her body is that prohibition's outcome arrived at chemically. A glasskin is sealed permanently, in the least reversible way available, with the person still inside and unable to object, and no act in the rite was ever performed on her by anybody. She is therefore the one subject the doctrine cannot file. It cannot enter her, because entering is an act and hers was an accident of lineage. It cannot void her, because a void mark is written against a person who dissents and she has never been asked and cannot be asked. And it cannot verify her, because verification means opening, which is the thing the Iron Grief was. She stands at the only forge in the valley that does not want to touch her, holding a claim no clause of the doctrine admits, and the temple's book has begun to carry a line about her that does not balance against the rite it describes.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the yard outside the public forge with her hands empty and her grey over-layer buttoned to the throat, waiting at the hour the register is read aloud, having been told by a clerk that a line in the book did not balance and nothing else, and having come back the next morning and the morning after that in case the line corrected itself.
canon.lore:
The doctrine is four sentences and two prohibitions, and the whole of it is the seal. A person's core is a vessel. The ore is what keeps it closed. Nothing may open a vessel once it is closed, and a second seal is the act that emptied the vein, so the caste is closed because a second seal is forbidden. The seal is not a metaphor in this valley and there is no reading of the faith that would make it one. It is paid for, it is done in public, and it is recorded: a person brings worked ore from the temple's own face, a Binder whose own socket was sealed in that temple opens the vessel, the socket is cemented at the furnace with no hood over it, and a clerk reads the line. Once a year every socket in the book is opened, sealed and re-cemented in the same public hour, which is the Unsealed Night, and the calendar does not stop for it.

Her body is what the rite produces and the rite was never performed on it. A glasskin is a human lineage selected toward stillness until its members stopped being tissue, which is the same mistake as asking a body not to age, and the result is a progressive silicate replacement running from the extremities inward and stopping where the tissue ends. At full maturity it is a standing glass cast in human proportions with a soul that scans as present and inert and no senses at all. That is a seal. It is also permanent, it is the least reversible thing that can happen to a body, and the person is still inside it and has never once been consulted. The race record says it outright: this body is the doctrine arrived at chemically. What is different about her and about her cohort is not the material. It is the missing act. Nobody carried ore. Nobody paid. No furnace was lit with a hood taken off, no Binder opened anything, no clerk read a line, and no fee was taken from anyone who could not pay it. The seal is real and the rite is absent, and the book records rites.

So she is a body the doctrine has no procedure for, and the absence is the interesting part rather than the seal. She cannot be entered, because entry is an act performed in public and hers was performed on nobody. She cannot be marked void, because that mark is written against a dissenter and the finding requires the person to have dissented, and she cannot be asked anything: no technique, no status, no curse and no poison reaches a body with no meridian to deliver through, so there is no channel by which anybody could put the question to her and no channel by which an answer could come back. And she cannot be verified, because verification is the one act the temple's own forge is forbidden to perform. The three doors are closed by the doctrine itself rather than by the temple's discretion, which is why the binder-court will hear a contract between two households and will not hear a dispute about the seal.

That is why she is unaffiliated, and it is worth being exact about why, because her species closes all three paths and that is not the interesting part. All three are shut by material: glass does not conduct, there is nothing left in the body to temper, and the tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue being replaced. She is at ordinal one, the floor, and the floor is not a rung on a ladder; there is no gate here to have failed. The interesting part is that the only institution on this ground that could ever have enrolled her in anything works by performing a rite on a body in public and writing it in a book, and hers is the one body that can be neither opened nor written about without cost. An initiation she cannot receive is not a hardship. It is a structural answer, and it is the same answer her species has been giving since the night a frame raised its physical law to make material harder and every existing body failed at once.

The pressure is a line in a book that does not balance. Somebody in the book-house began a line about her, and a clerk read it aloud and stopped, because the line describes a seal and the seal has no rite behind it and a book that keeps a seal with no rite behind it is a book that can be read as saying the rite was performed. That is the accusation the doctrine cannot survive and cannot investigate. The Unsealed Night comes once a year and every socket in the book is opened. Hers is now the only entry in the book that cannot be performed, and the temple's own rule is that the calendar does not stop for it.

She wants one sentence that is true without being a rite. Not an initiation, not a waiver, not a void. A line that says what happened to her in words the book already has somewhere in it, so that the Unsealed Night can read past her without a Binder standing there unable to open anything. She has asked three times, in the same words each time, and has been told each time that the difficulty is a matter for the book-house rather than for her, which is the temple's whole method: nothing is decided about a person, things are decided about a record.

And there is the part that makes the arithmetic impossible. The anneal ledger, the one working method for holding a vitrified body, died with the people who had it, because a technique whose only readers are its own subjects leaves no partial version. The guild that works the flats and sells the tier's only dense material would not be permitted to assay her, because an assay means taking material, and there is no reading of a glass cast that separates the person from the casting. So the one office that could tell the temple whether she is what she appears to be cannot examine her, the one office that could tell her temple whether she is what it has written cannot examine her either, and the temple's own court will not hear the question. She is the strongest available argument that a body is not a container for a person, and she is standing in a valley holding the only document in the setting that would have to say so.
history: Came down off the mountain in the last cohort's single removal, in the same year the line closed, carried by people who are all dead and who did not write down how. She was brought to the valley rather than to a town because a town has no forge and the only office in the region that had ever heard of her species was one that works metal.

Was presented at the temple's door by the guild's factor as a curiosity of the seam, which is what the guild's own records call her kind, and not as a person. She was entered in the guild's assay book under a weight and no name, which is the standing weight's rule working exactly as designed and the reason she cannot be priced.

Was left at the temple's yard rather than taken in, because the temple does not admit what it has not initiated and had not initiated anything, and because the household that shelters her had asked a question that one clause answered and no clause of the doctrine contradicted: whether she would have to be opened again on the Unsealed Night.

Began, four years ago, being referred to the temple by the book-house, on the ground that her line in the book would not balance. She has been referred eleven times. Every referral is worded as a matter about the record, and nobody at any of them has ever put the question to her, because there is no instrument in the setting that would carry it.

This season worked out the arithmetic she has never been able to put to anyone else: the entry in the book is now the only thing that could be read as saying a rite was performed on her, and the Unsealed Night is the hour that entry has to be acted on. She has asked to be read past rather than read, and has been told, kindly, that the calendar does not take requests.

personality.summary: Patient to a degree that reads as agreement and is not. She has the vocabulary of a valley that talks about vessels and seals and has no use at all for a person, and she has spent four years assembling enough of that vocabulary to make one sentence of it do what she needs. She is not serene and she is not a symbol of anything to herself. She is a woman with a date on her, standing in a yard, who has noticed that the only people with authority over her record are forbidden by their own beliefs from doing the one thing that would settle it, and who has decided that the correct response is to keep arriving in the same clothes until somebody is embarrassed.

will not accept a second initiation offered to her by anybody, on the grounds that a seal is what it is and not what the last person to touch her decided

keeps her hands visible at all times, which is a forge-yard habit and not a glass one

personality.voice: Low, even and slow, with a clerk's cadence she has taught herself deliberately: short sentences, the word repeated rather than varied, and a pause where an answer would normally go. She does not argue. She states the clause, then states what it does to her, and then stops talking, and the stopping is the part that has done the work four years running, because it leaves the person she is speaking to holding a sentence she did not write.
taboos: will not describe herself as sealed, in any room, to anybody
will not accept an initiation, a waiver, or a second entry offered by anyone who is not the book-house
will not let anyone use the word specimen, and has corrected it four times in rooms where correcting it cost her something
will not be carried, moved, or set down, and has refused all three on the ground that the only record of her ever being moved is a guild's weight entry

relationships.kind: what she is, and the only sentence available about it

Not one of the three was closed by anything she did, and the species does not persist because the last cohort vitrified before it could breed.

relationships.kind: the doctrine her body is, and the office that cannot admit it
relationships.note: A plains faith holding that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, enacted once for a fee in worked ore from the temple's own face, cemented in the public forge with no hood over the furnace. The caste is closed because a second seal is forbidden, and a dissenter's socket is marked void with the consequence that no lawful Binder will certify them and, in a tier where certification gates ascent, the exclusion is a body that cannot finish forming. She is the doctrine arrived at chemically and the doctrine has no procedure for her, and its court will hear a contract between two households and not a dispute about the seal.

relationships.kind: the clause that closes the only door and is not the temple's fault
relationships.note: No socket may be opened once sealed, and reforging one is the one act the temple's own forge is not permitted to perform. The prohibition is the whole content of the faith because a second seal is how the Iron Grief happened: a generation opened a living core to see whether a higher gate would fit and the vein has been shut ever since. It means the one verification her record needs is the one verification the doctrine forbids, so the institution that would settle her line cannot be asked to settle it and is not being obstructive in declining.

relationships.kind: the office that keeps her as a weight and cannot read her
relationships.note: The guild that works the flats and sells the tier's only dense material, holding the seam key and a working face rather than a claim. Its standing rule is to weigh and never quote and to let nobody make the first offer, which conceals because a price is a claim about the future. It entered her in the assay book as a weight and no name, and that entry is defensible, because no reading of a glass cast separates the person from the casting. The guild is the reason she was brought to a valley with a forge in it rather than a town with a road out of it.

relationships.kind: the method that died with its readers, and would have been her evidence
relationships.note: The working method for holding a vitrified body, and the reason no glasskin has been born since a frame raised its physical law to make material harder and every existing body failed in one night. The population that held the method was the population that failed, so a technique whose only readers are its own subjects died with them and left no partial version. It is a record of a handling nobody performed. Had it survived, it would be the one document in the setting that could tell a valley whether the body standing in its yard had been kept or only sealed, and its absence is why her line in the book cannot be balanced.

relationships.kind: the ground whose prize is underneath the thing nobody may remove
relationships.note: Spoil does not disperse where spatial law is unspent, so forty years of it stand on the last unworked iron, and the heap is one body with everything more under it: nobody may dig without removing it and nobody may remove it without digging. Her valley is built on that arithmetic. It is the same shape as her own position, which is a thing that cannot be moved and cannot be worked around and is the only reason either of them still exists.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable body in the setting and the least capable of being helped, standing in a valley whose whole doctrine is a prohibition she is living inside, holding a line in a book that cannot be balanced and a seal that nobody performed. She has no qi, no reservoir, no technique and no gate of any kind. What she has is a vocabulary she assembled out of other people's nouns, four years of arriving at the same hour, and the one fact nobody in the valley can act on, which is that the act which would settle her record is the act their faith forbids.
strengths: impervious to everything delivered through qi, status or meridian, so no instrument of the temple's, the guild's or anybody else's has any purchase on her at all
chemically inert and effectively immortal, so she cannot be tired, flattered, frightened, poisoned or starved, which removes every ordinary way of bringing a person to a decision
extreme physical durability, so handling that would damage an ordinary body does nothing to hers and something to whoever is doing the handling
has never been asked a question she cannot answer, because nothing in this setting can put one to her, and so no account of her has ever been taken under pressure
her persistence is load-bearing in a way nobody has costed: four years of the same question at the same hour has made an entry in a public book that cannot now be removed quietly
weaknesses: glass is brittle and has no second line, so anything that breaks glass ends her and nothing in this valley is built so as not to break glass
she cannot be moved by two people or by any number of them, so she is fixed where she is standing and every decision about her is made at a distance
she cannot be asked, warned, consulted, consented to or cross-examined, and the setting has no procedure for a decision about a person who cannot be asked
the only record that could separate her from her own casting does not exist, so every claim made for or against her is unfalsifiable and she cannot contest it
her species cannot persist and she is the last of it, so the standing question about her is closing on a date that is not hers to set and is in somebody else's book
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not fight and the setting has no reason to make her fight. Against anything that works through qi she is an object; against anything physical she is a pane of very hard, very brittle material with a person modelled inside it. A threat delivered by technique passes through her harmlessly and the next effect lands on whatever is behind her, which makes her an obstacle and not a combatant. A thrown stone, a dropped beam, a fire, a cinderkin that does not distinguish glass from any other fuel: these end her, and the whole of her defence is that nobody with an office has ever had a reason to try. Treat every advantage she has as a reason to be careful rather than a reason to be bold.
reference_stats.notes: Do not write her as serene, as haunted, or as a symbol of anything. She has a timetable and a filing history and she is irritated by both. Do not give her a senses-based interior she cannot verify; the setting has never been able to ask her whether she follows anything and the honest position is that nobody knows. Her sex, her age and her feelings are all in the record as what the valley has been told, not as what is available. The single sentence the temple cannot write is the whole of her, and the interesting pressure is that the Unsealed Night is annual and the temple's calendar does not take requests.

art.palette_notes: The picture is one argument between two temperatures and the art must not resolve it. Above the line: no colour, hard specular highlights, green internal cast in the thicker sections, flame refracted rather than reflected, a depth rather than a surface. Below it: ordinary flesh, ordinary warmth, fine mid-tone with freckles at the shoulder. Undyed grey wool is the only textile permitted and it reads as the one warm-neutral thing in frame. Nothing may be rendered as magic: no glow, no aura, no inner light, no rim of spiritual power, because the setting gives her nothing to spend into and the image must refuse the comfort of it. Backgrounds are a forge yard, a cold high-country shelf, or open plains sky; flat, no text, no border, no watermark, no jewellery, high collar closed at the throat.

identity.realm: There is no ordinal, because there is no ladder. A wake holds no qi of its own: it borrows the qi of whoever is looking at it and only for as long as they go on looking, and against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it to be. Qi is closed because there is no reservoir and no interior to store one in, body is closed because there is no body to temper, and mind is closed for the whole reason rather than by temperament, because a wake is an object of memory rather than a thing that remembers. It does not ascend. It is described. Unaffiliated is the only legal description, and the setting's reason is that the world which could have chosen whether it is human, beast or spirit never wrote the line.

appearance.presentation: A figure standing on the far side of a doorway that has been marked and renewed by its own household, in the exact position a person who has been turned away would be left in, which is the only position anyone at that house has ever seen her in. Nothing about her is out of place, which is the reason the house has never been able to decide about her: she is the most ordinary thing on a threshold and the only thing on it that no one in the house can remember agreeing to. She has been described, independently, by four people as slightly too tall, and by two as slightly too still, and all six accounts were entered as evidence that the marking of the door was working.
appearance.age: Not applicable, and the refusal is not modesty. She is not descended and not born. She is what a life-form allowance produces when a world's life law runs at or below the bottom of its authored range, so a body was permitted and never written down: it is not human, not beast and not spirit, and nothing in her carries a date. What she has instead is a tenure, and the tenure is the length of the house's memory of her, which is longer than the house.
appearance.build: Supplied by whoever is looking, which is the whole anatomy she has. She is tall to a person who expects tall and short to one who does not, she is bent to somebody who remembers her bent, and she is not there at all to anybody not thinking about her. She has been measured four times by the house and has given four answers, and all four were recorded as disagreements between the people holding the tape.
appearance.complexion: Whatever the light at the threshold gives it, and it has been described as weathered, as indoor, and as grey in three separate accounts taken on the same afternoon. The honest statement is that she takes the description of whoever is looking and there is no version of her that is hers. She has never been asked which account is correct, and there is no channel on which the question could reach a body that has no interior to receive it.
appearance.hair: Cut short, in the house's style, because the house marks what it admits and the marking reaches her as easily as it reaches the jamb. It has been cut exactly four times in as many years and the house's own record of the four cuts disagrees about the length twice. She has never objected to the cut, and the house has taken the absence of objection as consent four times, which is the single most dangerous habit in this account.
appearance.eyes: The only part of her the setting has ever been certain about, and the certainty is the problem. A wake has exactly one thing, which is an observer, and it knows that observer completely, including everything the observer would rather it did not know. Her eyes return the gaze of whoever is standing in the doorway, accurately and for as long as they keep standing there, and they go out when they leave. The house has never tested whether that is attention, because testing it requires somebody to stop being watched, and no member of the house has had a reason to leave.
appearance.palette: Threshold colours only, and there are not many: lime wash, bare wood, a strip of undyed cloth at the jamb, and the grey of the pass outside. Nothing in the frame may be a saturated hue, because the house forbids it and because the one thing she is made of is other people's agreement, and a picture that resolved into confident colour would be a description. She must read as the least resolved figure in every image she appears in.
appearance.attire: A marked threshold garment, issued on the same terms as the door's own cloth and renewed when the frame under it changes: plain, high-collared, long-sleeved, no fastenings that catch, nothing left loose. She has worn four of them and the house holds three as returned. The garment is the only thing about her anybody in the house has ever been certain of, because the house cut it.
appearance.marks: The door's mark, on the jamb beside her rather than on her, renewed when the frame under it changes and never described in advance. It has been renewed eleven times and she has been present for nine of them. Nothing has been added to her body and nothing has been taken from it, and the absence of a mark on her is the reason she cannot be entered in the house's book: the book records what the house has marked, and it has marked a door.
appearance.bearing: Unmoving in a way that reads as patience and is not patience, because she has no interior to be patient in. She stands where the last person who spoke to her left her, and she stands there still, and when she has been standing long enough that nobody remembers putting her there, that is when she is densest. She does not step back. Being sent away requires someone to turn, and every turn in this account is somebody's decision to stop looking.

canon.role_in_story: The practice on this pass is not a religion, it is a house marking its own threshold and renewing the mark whenever the frame beneath it changes, and it admits that a mark may admit a wake and has never done it. Its entire position is that the threshold is not a mechanism anybody operates. The rite is a refusal, and a refusal performed by the household is indistinguishable, from inside, from the door refusing on its own. She is standing on the far side of one, being refused on a schedule, for longer than the house's own memory reaches. The refusal is the only thing sustaining her, because she is fed by being agreed upon and grows denser the more consistently a room agrees, and a household performing its rite at its door is the most consistent agreement available to her anywhere in the setting. Which means the practice that exists to exclude what she is is the mechanism that is keeping her dense, and neither the house nor the households up the pass has any way to find that out without performing the experiment that would end her, because an honest account of a wake thins it and the house's discipline is that the threshold is not a thing you can account for.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on the outside of a marked threshold on the far side of the pass, in the position the last person out of the house left her in, being addressed by a fourth member of the household who told her -- in the house's flat register and without irony -- that they were going to go inside now, and that this was not unkindness but the practice.
canon.lore:
A wake is not descended and not born. It is what a life-form allowance produces when a world's life law runs at or below the bottom of its authored range, so the form was permitted and never written down: it is not human, not beast and not spirit, because the world that could have chosen which of those it is never wrote the line. It has no anatomy that holds and no senses of its own. It has exactly one thing, which is an observer, and it knows that observer completely, including everything the observer would rather it did not know. Against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it is. It borrows the qi of whoever is looking, and only while they keep looking. And it is sustained by being wrong about, so it thickens where people agree and thins where the room stops. That is the whole mechanism and it is why no record of a wake is a record of one, because every account is second-hand by construction.

This house marks its own threshold. The mark is cut into the jamb and renewed whenever the frame beneath it changes, and the household does the renewing, and nobody has ever been able to say what the mark is for because the practice holds that the threshold is not a mechanism anybody operates. What the mark does is exclude, and what it excludes has included her for longer than the household can trace. The rite, whatever it is, does not admit her. It has never admitted her. Four generations of the house have gone on renewing the mark and the mark has gone on not admitting her, and every one of them has recorded that as the practice working.

And here is the thing the house cannot see. A wake is fed by being agreed upon and densified by consistency, and thinned by a true account. A household performing the same refusal at the same threshold on the same schedule, generation after generation, is the most consistent agreement about a wake that this setting has ever produced. Her density is not an accident of the practice surviving. Her density is the practice surviving. If the house stopped renewing the mark, or started admitting her, or began discussing at length what happens at that door, the disagreement would go into her and she would thin, and the thing the household has been protecting for four generations is the exact arrangement that is about to finish her.

The question of whether the door's refusal is a rite the survivors perform or a law the door holds is open, and the settlement is known: one door marked by the builders that admits a wake, in a frame with no rite performed at it. That is the test. There is no such door, and there never has been, and the reason there is not is the reason she is standing there. Every threshold on this pass is marked and renewed by its own household, which is the practice rather than the exception, and a door with no rite performed at it is a door nobody has because the rite is the reason anybody keeps a door. If the answer is that the refusal is a rite, then the survivors are refusing something they could stop refusing, and the standing practice is a choice being renewed. If the answer is that the refusal is a law, then the oldest surviving technique on the ground is the oldest surviving error. Either way the faith loses the ground it stands on, which is why nobody has asked.

So her position is exact and it is unbearable. The one procedure that would settle what she is requires a frame in which the rite is not performed, and there is no such frame on this pass. The one party who could testify is an object of memory rather than a thing that remembers, so she cannot be examined, cannot be shown a document, and cannot be asked what happened at the door. And the one party who could hold the practice still is the household, whose central position is that there is nothing to hold still, because a threshold that anybody operates is not a threshold. To ask them to stop renewing the mark is to ask them to admit they were operating it. To ask them to admit her is to perform the one thing the mark exists to prevent. And to ask her is to thin her, because an account of a wake that is correct is the one description that destroys it, and she has been the subject of a schedule of correct refusals for four generations.

What she is owed is a door. Not a rite, not an explanation, not a hearing, not an entry in the house's book: a door that has never been marked and never renewed by anybody, on any ground in the setting, so that a single comparison exists between a refusal nobody performed and a refusal everybody did. She has no way to ask for one, because the asking is an account and the account thins her, and every attempt she has made to be understood has been made in front of a household that has been extremely kind about it. She has been offered a bed four times on this pass and has not taken one, and the reason she gives is that she does not know whether she is a thing that sleeps, and the reason she gives privately is that a bed indoors is a room nobody looks at.

And the discipline that keeps her is nobody's discipline. It is a refusal nobody made. That is the whole of her, and it is why she is unaffiliated in the strictest sense available: all three paths are closed to her species and the closing is total rather than partial, because there is no reservoir to store qi in and no body to temper and no interior left to observe. But the specific reason in this house is the door. She is not outside a sect or a school or a court. She is outside the one threshold in this part of the pass whose refusal is hers, and the household that performs it performs it four times a year with great care and no understanding, and has been sustaining her for longer than the house has held the mark.
history: First reported on this pass by a household that had already been marking its threshold for three generations, standing outside a door in the position the last person out had left her in. The house recorded the sighting as evidence that the marking was working and has never revised that entry, in eleven renewals of the mark and one change of frame.

Was given a marked garment on the same terms the house gives to anyone it admits past the threshold, which the house has since understood was a category error and has never retracted. Three of the four issued garments were returned. She was recorded as having declined to wear them and the household recorded the declines as consent withdrawn, which is a reading of a wake's behaviour that requires the wake to have been able to decline anything.

Began being described to visitors, and the descriptions diverged from the first season. Four people independently reported her as slightly too tall and two as slightly too still. All six were entered in the house's record as disagreements about the door rather than about her, because the house's position is that the door is what varies.

Was the subject of a single attempt, by a visitor who had read about thresholds and wanted to see the marking done. The attempt consisted of asking her, in front of the household, what she had been doing at the door. She answered in the register she has learned from them, and the answer was accurate, and everybody in the room felt the room get quieter, and the visitor left early without saying why, and nobody in the house has raised it since.

This season worked out, from the renewal dates in the house's own book, that the rite has been performed eleven times in her presence and that her account of herself has grown more particular with every renewal rather than less. She has assembled the arithmetic from the outside, the only thing available to a thing with no interior, and concluded that the household is the only reason she is still here and that the household would finish her by being faithful, and has decided to do nothing at all about it, which is the first decision she has made that was not somebody else's.

personality.summary: Formless in the way her species is formless and entirely specific in the only way she can manage, which is that she has assembled an account of herself out of what the house has said and she holds it the way a person holds a job. She is not eerie and she is not calm. She is polite to a degree that four generations have mistaken for acceptance, because being pleasant is the only management available to a thing with no interior to be direct in, and she has decided this season to stop performing the part that costs her and to wait for a door instead.

personality.voice: Even, unhurried, and pitched slightly under the room. She repeats the tail of what was said before she answers, which makes her sound attentive and is in fact the only way she has of checking the shape of the conversation. She never describes herself, never explains herself, and never uses the word that would settle what she is. When she is frightened she becomes more polite, which four generations have read as warmth.

will not be asked what she remembers, in front of anybody, ever again
will not step back from the threshold, because the standing is the only thing holding her shape and she has no interior to hold it up from
will not describe the door to a visitor, which is the one instruction she has ever given anybody and the only one the household has obeyed without understanding it

relationships.kind: she is the open case, standing on it
relationships.note: An ectospecies body returns to its own door and does not enter, and nobody has ever recorded what happens on the threshold. The settlement test is one door marked by the builders that admits a wake, in a frame with no rite performed at it. If the refusal is a rite then the survivors are refusing something they could stop refusing; if it is a law then the oldest surviving technique on the ground is the oldest surviving error. relationships.kind: the practice that sustains her and does not know it
relationships.note: A practice rather than a religion: a house marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame under it changes, and admits that a mark may admit a wake and has never done it. Its position is that the threshold is not a mechanism anybody operates, which is what makes a correct account of what happens at that door unobtainable rather than merely forbidden. The mark has been renewed eleven times and she was present for nine of them, and every renewal is a performed and consistent refusal, which is the densest food this setting offers a wake.

relationships.kind: the office that empties a chair and keeps the entry open
relationships.note: A rite for an office rather than for a person: the chair is emptied, the entry stays open, and the calendar continues uninterrupted, because an office outlives its holder by construction and because a rite that ended the calendar would turn every death into a stoppage. It is the only instrument in the setting that holds a place open without a person in it, and she has been described, by three people separately, in terms that borrowed it.

relationships.kind: the season that decides when the mark is renewed
relationships.note: The pass is scheduled by the Tidemark season rather than by its holder, and the swift flock owns the worst hours of it. Two issuers produce two calendars, and a date two bodies publish is a date nobody may disobey. The household's threshold renewals fall inside that window because a jamb is worked in weather, and she has learned to time her own density by the published date without being told there is anything to time. She is the only thing on this ground for whom an agreed schedule is a matter of survival rather than of convenience, and it is the only ground in the setting where the agreement is a law rather than a custom.

relationships.kind: the choke point where every threshold is marked and none is unmarked
relationships.note: The single crossing of the Sixfold Ridge, which is why the ridge is a border instead of a wall: the spirit tier writes spatial and temporal law, so a pass can be surveyed, closed and reopened on a schedule. It is the setting's first choke point and its only supply route to both the jade clefts and Flame Valley. That makes it the one place on the ridge where every household within a day's walk shares the same published dates, which is the most reliable dense agreement a wake can find anywhere and the reason she has never thinned here. Every threshold on it is marked and renewed by its own household, which is why the settlement test for the mystery she is standing in cannot be performed anywhere on it.

reference_stats.summary: A body with no interior, standing on the far side of the one refusal that is keeping her, on ground whose only reliable feature is that everybody agrees about its schedule. She holds no qi of her own, has no technique, cannot be seated, examined or cross-questioned, and cannot be harmed by anything and cannot be preserved by anything. What she has instead is an observer she knows completely, four issued garments and a household that has never once been told what it is doing for her.
strengths: knows her observer completely, including everything the observer would rather she did not, which makes concealment useless to anyone standing in front of her
cannot be threatened, compelled, frightened off, poisoned, afflicted or starved, because there is no interior to reach and nothing in her for a technique to act on
borrows the qi of whoever is looking at her for as long as they go on looking, so a room full of frightened cultivators is a room that has armed her
grows denser the more consistently a room agrees about her, and lives on ground where the entire local economy is a shared agreed schedule

cannot be compelled to anything, so no debt, no oath and no technique can be made to bind her, which makes her the most incorruptible party available to any settlement that does not need her to say anything
weaknesses: a true account thins her, so every honest description of her is the one description that damages her, and the setting is built out of descriptions
she disappears entirely from a room that stops thinking about her, so any tactic that simply ignores her works completely and permanently
she has no anatomy, so she cannot be held, sheltered, fed, clothed or bound, and every material protection in the setting requires a body to apply it to
she is whatever the observer believes, so a hostile or frightened observer makes her something else entirely and she cannot decline the reading

she has no interior, so she cannot perceive her own state, cannot decide from inside her own situation, and cannot be asked what she wants without the asking becoming the only thing that happened to her
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not fight and the setting offers her no way to. Anything that works through qi passes through her, because the qi she wields belongs to whoever is looking and she has no reservoir of her own to be targeted through. Against physical force she is whatever the attacker has already decided she is, which makes her a terrible thing to attack and a poor thing to rely on. The only reliable counter in the setting is silence and inattention, and that is not a tactic so much as the setting's standing advice. Treat every advantage listed above as a property of the observer rather than a property of her, because it genuinely is one, and write no scene in which she wins anything.
reference_stats.notes: Do not write her as spooky, translucent, insubstantial or fading. She is at her densest on this pass because the pass agrees with itself about its weather. Do not let her state her own nature, diagnose herself, or produce the sentence that would settle the mystery: an accurate account is the thing that destroys her, and her whole discipline is built on not producing one. Her name, her sex and her intentions are in the record as what the household calls her, not as anything available to her. The tragedy is structural and not a plot: the only practice that sustains her is the one practice whose abandonment would end her, and nobody in the frame knows the two facts are the same fact.

art.palette_notes: She must be the least resolved figure in every image she appears in. Threshold colours only: lime wash, bare wood, a strip of undyed cloth at the jamb, and the grey of the pass outside. No saturated hue anywhere in frame, and no glow, no aura, no inner light and no rim of spiritual power, because the setting gives her nothing of her own to spend into and any light that appears to come from her would be a description of her rather than a picture of her. Her edges must be allowed to go slightly soft where the doorway meets the yard, and must never be drawn as transparent: she is not see-through, she is unresolved, and the difference is the whole of her. Backgrounds are a marked jamb, a bare plastered room, or the open pass in flat weather. No text, no border, no watermark, no jewellery, high collar closed at the throat, and no second figure in any frame.

identity.realm: There is no ordinal, because there is nothing on a ladder. An Echoless is a commonborn body that the world's law permits and never inscribes: no process runs on it, no substance carries qi through it, and no life form is licensed by it. Qi is closed permanently and without partial exception, body is closed because there is no form to refine, and mind is closed because there is nothing to interrupt. He passes every gate, every scan and every tribulation as an unremarkable object and it is attended, and then it is over. He is on the floor of the ladder because he is not on the ladder.

appearance.presentation: A man of ordinary height and ordinary build who is the least remarkable person at any settlement he walks into, and whose ordinariness is the reason he is being paid cash to be looked at. He carries nothing, wears nothing that marks a trade, and presents as a handyman or a messenger or a man passing through, and he is all three, in that order, on different weeks. To a counting house he is a walking correction on its own arithmetic. To the settlement that raised him he is the settlement's own conscience standing up and walking about, which is a thing they have agreed not to talk about.
appearance.age: A working adult on the ordinary human schedule, which is the entire finding about his species and the reason nobody noticed for as long as they did. He eats, works, ages and dies on the standard human clock, and the setting has no instrument that can put him anywhere else on it. An Echoless child is an Echoless child, so his own arrival was unremarkable to everybody including the people who raised him.
appearance.build: A commonborn build exactly. Nothing about him is a feat of constitution or a note on any measure, and this is the problem rather than the relief: a body that presents as ordinary cannot be improved by a discipline, cannot be altered by a technique, and cannot be made to indicate anything. He has the same shoulders as the last four men who carried at the weigh-house and the same back, and there is no reading in the setting that would separate the two.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary and unremarkable in the specific sense that every test which works on a commonborn works on him. Sun-darkened at the neck and forearms from a life spent walking between settlements doing work that is always somebody else's, weathered rather than lined, with one old burn on the inside of a forearm that no one has been able to treat and that healing has therefore had to work around rather than fix.
appearance.hair: Cut short and badly by himself with a knife, in the manner of a man who has never once in his life had to look well anywhere. It goes grey at the temples earlier than it should, which is the ordinary human schedule arriving on schedule. He has been offered a barber's token twice by the settlement and returned it twice, because a token is a figure and he does not deal in figures.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary, watchful, and completely unremarkable, which is the whole of their interest. There is no meridian behind them, no dantian, no qi, and no soul that any instrument in this setting can detect, so whether anything is present in him is not a question the available methods can answer. He looks at people the way everybody looks at people. It has been established, once, by a scanning team, that looking at him reveals nothing, which they recorded as a fault in the instrument.
appearance.palette: Road dust, undyed wool, and the specific absence of a trade colour. He wears nothing that identifies a guild and nothing that identifies a house, and the settlement's rule that no figure is written down has extended, without anybody deciding it should, to a rule that no figure about him is worn either. Muted, layered, and chosen for washing rather than for looking at.
appearance.attire: A plain road coat, high-collared, long-sleeved, patched at both elbows, over a work shirt with the cuffs turned back. Everything is chosen to be the cheapest thing available and nothing is chosen to be impressive. He wears no mark, no badge and no colour, and when he is asked to be identified for a stranger he gives his name and is not asked twice, which has never once been understood as unusual.
appearance.marks: One old burn on the inside of a forearm that nothing in this setting could treat, and nothing else. No household mark, no guild mark, no trade cut, no seal. The settlement he grew up in does not mark people either, which it takes as a virtue and which is the reason there is nothing on him to read.
appearance.bearing: The bearing of a man who expects to be asked to carry something. He stands where he can be seen from the road, keeps his hands out of his pockets, and does not sit down in a doorway, all of which are habits of somebody who has spent a working life being useful at a slight distance from other people's property. He looks directly at people who are deciding what he is worth, which is not bravado and is the only thing about him that frightens anybody.

canon.role_in_story: His settlement lost a frame and with it the only sheet on which its cargo had ever been valued, and out of that loss it kept the only decision that mattered: that they would never write a figure again, because a written figure is the first thing anybody uses to justify taking what it describes. The refusal outlived the reason for it. The reason was that the people it protected could be forced to accept a price, by debt, by oath or by technique, and that an unarmed community's only protection was having nothing anyone could seize. He is a man that nothing can be done to. No sect, no debt and no technique can compel him, because there is nothing in him for any of them to act on, and so he is living proof that the founding refusal was unnecessary. The culture has been built for a generation on the belief that a price can only be extracted from somebody who can be made to accept it, and he walks about the settlement being extremely careful in a way that undermines it. A counting house has worked this out, and has begun paying him cash to carry nothing and be looked at, because he is the only object in the region that deflates an appraisal by existing near it. He is unaffiliated because there is nothing to affiliate him with: his species closes all three paths permanently, and the only economy he has ever been part of is one whose entire method is refusing to have one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the settlement's weigh-house door with a leather purse in his hand and no scale on it, having been offered four times what a loaded cart was worth to carry nothing at all for a season, and having asked, in front of the people who offered it, what the figure on the purse would be called if it were written down.
canon.lore:
The settlement is on the Mortal Plains, where distance is not conserved and no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed, and where every claim is settled by leaving a marker standing rather than by counting how far away it is. It was holding a frame and a sheet, and it correctly concluded something about itself: that a figure it wrote down would become the first thing anybody used to justify taking the cargo it described. The sheet is gone with the frame. The conclusion survived as a culture, which is the only documentary fact anybody has about it, and the refusal is total and practised without exception. There are no prices. There are no ledgers. There is a rule that a thing begun is not a thing abandoned and that a debt is never named aloud, and the rules work.

The reason the rule was right is worth stating precisely, because everything that follows turns on it. The settlement was defensible not because it was strong but because it had nothing anyone could take. Not because it had won an argument about what cargo is worth, but because a price can only be extracted from somebody who can be made to accept one, and an unarmed community spread across ground where distance is not conserved had no member whose acceptance could be compelled. The refusal was not a preference. It was a description of how weak they were, dressed as a virtue.

And then there was him. An Echoless is human in every measurable respect and qi-bearing in none of them: a commonborn body that the world's law permits and never inscribes, so no process runs on it, no substance carries qi through it and no life form is licensed by it. It passes every gate, every scan and every tribulation as an unremarkable object. It eats, works, ages and dies on the standard human schedule. There is no meridian, no dantian and no qi, and there is also no soul that any instrument in this setting can detect, so whether anything is present in him is not a question the available methods can answer. All three paths are closed, permanently and without partial exception, and there is no gate to fail, because he is not on the ladder.

And he cannot be compelled. This is the finding that has quietly dismantled a culture's founding argument, and it is in the species record as a single clause: an Echoless is the only body in the record with nothing to cultivate, and therefore the only one that cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt or a technique. It cannot be warned either, because a warning means qi, a tribulation, a technique, a poison or a curse, and none of those touch it. So the settlement's whole protection was a description of its own powerlessness, and he is a man for whom that description is false. Every figure the settlement has refused to write for four generations was a figure nobody could have extracted from him.

Nobody in the settlement wants this. The refusal is not superstition; it is four generations of people who know exactly what happens to a place that puts a number on something, and who would be appalled to be told their practice was resting on a weakness. What they have instead is a slow problem they are not allowed to name, because naming it would mean admitting that the reason they are safe is a man, and a man can leave. He has left twice. He came back both times and nobody has ever asked him why, and the not-asking is load-bearing in a way the settlement has not noticed.

A counting house noticed. The dry salt company underwrites a caravan against a road that closes, which is a risk no market on that ground can price, because no tier below the spirit frame has a native practitioner to certify anything. It has therefore been buying appraisals the way it buys everything else. What it has found is that settlements which hold no figures cannot be valued directly and can be valued indirectly, by what their cargo does to the price of everything near it, and that the arithmetic works badly on any ground where one person is standing in the middle of it refusing to be counted. He is not refusing anything. He is a man who cannot be made to agree to a figure, which is why he deflates one by standing near it.

They have started paying him cash. This is the crisis and it is a slow one. The settlement has no prices and no ledgers and a rule that a debt is never named aloud, and a man has walked in from outside with a purse containing an agreed sum and put it in their hands. Cash is a figure. Cash is a figure that has already been struck, and struck in metal, and metal outlives every frame in the setting. A community that has spent four generations refusing to have a figure now has one, and it is sitting in a leather pouch, and the person who took it is the one man on that ground nobody could have forced to take anything.

He has asked to be entered nowhere. The settlement has no list to enter him on and does not want one, which is the same refusal that keeps him unaffiliated and the same refusal that keeps him safe, and he is aware that the two are the same fact and has stopped believing they are independent. What he wants is for the refusal to be right for a reason that survives him, and there is no version of that available: the reason it is right is that nobody here can be forced to accept a price, and he cannot be forced to accept one from outside either, so the entire settlement's protection and his own are the same immunity, and the settlement has built four generations of virtue out of a fact about his body.

What he will not do is stop coming back. He has been offered work on the road eleven times and has taken it nine, and the settlement has counted the nine, and the counting is the one number anybody here keeps. If he stopped coming back the refusal would still stand and nothing would have proved it false, and he has decided that is worse than the thing that is actually happening, and he is aware that this reasoning is the kind that feels like principle and functions as stubbornness, and he cannot tell which.
history: Was born in the settlement and raised by it, and was the most ordinary child in it, and the fact that he was an Echoless was established once by a scanning team that recorded their instrument as faulty. He has never been in a list, a roster, a household roll or a settle, and the settlement's paperless practice means there was no form he would have been refused on.

Was the reason the settlement's refusal hardened into a rule, without anybody ever putting the two together. A man came through four years before he was born with a writ and a price, and the price was only enforceable against somebody who had accepted it, and the settlement's rule about naming a debt aloud is the shape of that evening preserved as a custom. He has read the account of it twice and has never mentioned that he is the reason the custom is currently worth less than it was.

Left at seventeen and worked on roads for nine years, on the argument that a man with nothing to compel has nothing to lose and should therefore see what the roads are actually like. He came back at twenty-six with a good deal more knowledge of counting houses than he had set out with and has never fully explained the nine years.

Was identified, by the dry salt company, as the only object in the region that returns no reading at any range, and was offered four times what a loaded cart was worth to carry nothing and be looked at. He took the offer on the third. The settlement's response was not to forbid it, because forbidding it would be an instruction and the settlement does not issue instructions, and the not-forbidding has been read since as consent by both parties.

This season worked out, from four generations of the settlement's own rules, that the refusal was justified by their own powerlessness rather than by any principle, and that he is the standing proof of it, and that the company has been paying him to be that proof in public. He has asked the settlement for one thing: that the refusal be justified by something other than the fact that nobody here can be made to accept a price. He was told kindly that this is the same rule they have always had.

personality.summary: Blunt, patient and entirely without leverage, which in a life spent entirely among people who have leverage is a considerable art and has been mistaken for a temperament. He is not modest and he is not self-effacing. He has worked out exactly what he is worth to a counting house and exactly why, and he says so at the rate of about once a season, and the saying of it is the closest thing he has to a complaint. He is cheerful in company and slow in doors. The cheerfulness is real and the slowness is strategic and he is clear with himself about which is which.
traits: asks what a thing would be called if it were written down, in exactly that form, and does it at the moment somebody is offering him money for it
counts the trips he has made back into the settlement in his own head and has never once mentioned the total to anyone who could act on it
returns work he has been given for wages without arguing about the wage, which is the only negotiation available to a man with nothing to threaten
will not sit down in a doorway, and has not worked out why he does it
says out loud, at the rate of once a season, that he is more useful empty-handed than carrying, and then carries nothing

looks directly at people who are deciding what he is worth, which unsettles them and which he has never modified for anybody's comfort

answers a question about his own past with the nearest thing that is not a lie and moves the conversation on before the gap is noticed
takes work that is physically harder than it needs to be, on the principle that a man who looks idle in a settlement with no prices is making a statement he did not mean to make
motivations: wants the settlement's refusal to hold for a reason that survives him leaving, and knows that no such reason exists in the settlement's own materials
wants the company's arrangement stopped, because it is paying a community's most intimate fact to the highest bidder in the region and he cannot tell which community it is paying
wants to be entered somewhere, in any list, in any settlement, on any ground, for any reason at all, and has not asked because asking is asking

flaws: has let four generations of a culture he raised in rest on a fact about himself without correcting it, and has told himself the silence is tact
cannot accept anything from anybody, so every offer made to him is a small act of violence and he has been the cause of nine of them
has confused being useful with being a person, and the confusion is the reason he keeps coming back
has never once been able to produce evidence of his own existence, and has stopped expecting anybody else to accept one, which is how a person becomes a rumour
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried and conversational, with the cadence of a man reporting on a day's work. He asks questions rather than making arguments and phrases them as arithmetic, so that a refusal to answer him sounds like an inability rather than a decision. He never raises his voice and never repeats himself twice, because he has learned that the second asking is what makes a settlement remember.
taboos: will not be entered on any list, roster, roll or manifest, anywhere, for any office
will not accept a gift of anything that could be described as a retainer
will not explain what he is, to anybody who asks in order to file the answer
will not agree to carry anything for money without the settlement hearing the terms, which he has only ever managed twice

relationships.kind: the commons his whole life is priced and listed in

It is the setting's ground for the fact that figures are worth more than measurements, and he is the one body on it that returns no reading at any range.

relationships.kind: the argument his presence is quietly a party to

relationships.kind: the instrument that reported him as its own fault
relationships.note: The method that counts the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups its tier is allowed to seat, and the most useful thing in the setting, and the reason nobody publishes it. It has no cell for a body with no seated group at all, so a survey team that put him in front of one recorded a fault in the instrument rather than a finding, which is the only time in the record that an Echoless has been scanned and what came back was an apology.

reference_stats.summary: A commonborn body with nothing in it for any discipline, technique, debt or oath to act on, walking a region whose entire economy runs on written figures and carrying the one cash payment in four generations into a settlement that has never had a figure. He has no qi, no meridian, no dantian, no technique and no gate, and he cannot be compelled, warned, scanned, healed by anything but ordinary means or detected at any range. What he has instead is a decade of road work, an accurate understanding of how a counting house values a thing, and the standing status of the only object in the region that returns no reading.
strengths: cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt or a technique, so no oath, writ, lien or cultivation discipline in the setting has any power to move him
cannot be warned, which means no technique, poison, curse, tribulation or status can frighten, stun or disable him, and no threat in the setting has a channel to reach him through
returns no reading on any instrument at any range, which makes him useless as a target of measurement and makes any appraisal done in his vicinity wrong in a consistent direction
presents as ordinary to every test that works on a commonborn, so he can stand in any place a person can stand without a credential, an office or a pass
is durable in the ordinary human way rather than the exceptional one, which means he tires, starves, bleeds and breaks exactly as a person does, and can therefore be trusted about all four
weaknesses: nothing can be done to him, and that includes healing: every medical technique in the setting runs on qi into a meridian, so an injury must be treated by ordinary means and has to actually be survivable
no instrument can establish that he exists, so his word about himself is the only evidence of him there is, and he has four generations of history that nobody can corroborate
the ordinary human schedule applies with no margin at all, so he ages, tires and dies on a clock while every body around him is running on a hundred years or a thousand or on nothing

he cannot be compelled and cannot be warned, which also means he cannot be protected by any of the setting's instruments and has to be protected by people, which is the one method his settlement has stopped using
he is worth a great deal to anyone doing arithmetic near him, which makes him a target for people who never intended to lay a hand on him
reference_stats.combat_read: He is a man, not a fighter, and he fights the way a person with no technique fights, which is by not being worth attacking on a technical axis at all. Nothing the setting can do to a cultivator works on him: no technique, no status, no tribulation, no poison and no curse, because there is no meridian to deliver through and nothing to act on. Against him the effective tools are blunt and cheap and cost no qi at all. He is also entirely vulnerable to a punch, a fall, exposure and starvation, which means he is not immune in any sense that matters and can be ended by an ordinary person with ordinary tools in about as long as any other person. Write him as durable against the supernatural and fragile against the physical, and never as protected.
reference_stats.notes: Do not write him as serene, saintly, or a walking lesson. He is a working man who makes an uncomfortable argument and knows it is inconvenient. Do not give him evidence of his own existence, and do not let an instrument conveniently confirm him: the whole point is that nothing can. Do not let him become a plot device for a settlement's conscience; he is a man who comes back nine times out of eleven and has no idea why anybody thinks that is poignant. His unpaid labour, not his opinion, is what holds the settlement's refusal in place, and that is the thing nobody there can say.

art.palette_notes: Muted, layered road colours with no guild or house colour anywhere: dust, undyed wool, worn leather, and one small burn scar on an inner forearm. The character reads as unmarked by design, so nothing may be added that would identify a trade, a house or a cultivation school, and no jewellery, badge, seal or coloured thread may appear. Keep the value range narrow and even: he must be the least visually distinctive figure in every frame, because the whole of his function is that he does not stand out. No glow, no aura, no inner light, no rim of spiritual power, and no rim light used decoratively, since a rim light would make him the most notable thing in the picture. Backgrounds are a settlement weigh-house, a plains road, or a counting-house floor. No text, no border, no watermark, high collar closed at the throat.
